t: A Tagalog settlement called Maynila stood on the Pasig River by the 13th century and was conquered by Spain in 1571, after which Manila was the capital of the Spanish East Indies for about three centuries.
Its galleon trade with Acapulco linked Asia and the Americas, and its streets held Chinese, Spanish, Mexican, Japanese and many other peoples, with the walled city of Intramuros at the centre.

Britain held the city from 1762 to 1764, the United States took it in 1898, and in 1945 a battle of about a month destroyed most of it before it was rebuilt as the capital of an independent Philippines.
dyk: In 1603 Manila was home to 25,000 Chinese, 14,437 native families and 3,528 mixed Spanish-Filipino families, and a Spanish Jesuit wrote that because so many languages met there the confessional in Manila was the most difficult in the world.
ev: A fortified Tagalog settlement called Maynila is said to exist on the site
Miguel López de Legazpi takes Maynila and begins building Spanish Manila on its ruins
The Chinese warlord Limahong attacks the city and is defeated
An earthquake destroys much of the stone-and-brick city, and another does so in 1677
British forces capture Manila and hold it until 1764
Spain cedes the Philippines to the United States after the Battle of Manila
The Battle of Manila destroys most of the city and civilians are killed in the Manila massacre
The People Power Revolution ends the rule of Ferdinand Marcos

f.founded: A fortified Tagalog polity called Maynila existed on the site by 1258, according to genealogical research; the Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi began the walled city of Intramuros on its ruins in 1571.
f.where: On the eastern shore of Manila Bay on the island of Luzon, in the Philippines, with the Pasig River flowing through the middle of the city.
f.known: The Tagalog polity of Maynila; the Spanish capital of the East Indies; the Manila–Acapulco galleon trade; Intramuros and Binondo; the British occupation of 1762 to 1764; the Katipunan and the Philippine Revolution; the Battle of Manila of 1945; the People Power Revolution of 1986
f.today: Manila is the capital of the Philippines and its second most populous city, at the centre of the Metro Manila region.
